title: Edge routing fallback matrix & simulation runbook
content:
Summary:
This document captures an operational playbook that sits inside architecture notes for the routing/control-plane layer. It focuses on decision matrices for edge routing, multi-region failover, and safe mitigation steps for incidents that originate from routing policy failures, control plane instability, or regional capacity drops. The goal is to be prescriptive during incidents while documenting the rationale for each tactical choice so on-call engineers can act quickly and reviewers can replay what happened.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform SREs, platform-engineering on-call, release engineers, and solutions engineers who operate Dedicated/Private clusters.
- Scope: regional routing policies, control-plane decisioning (policy evaluation and push), traffic shaping at the edge, model-variant fallback rules, and multi-region failover criteria. Not covered: lower-level GPU scheduler internals or application-layer retries (except where they interact with routing).

High-level architecture notes (quick refresher):
- Data plane (edge proxies + inference workers) handles per-request routing using pre-fetched policy bundles.
- Control plane is authoritative for policy pushes, rollout orchestration, and health scoring. It sends incremental deltas to proxies and keeps a registry of region capacities and model variants.
- Decision points: latency-first vs cost-first routing, regional affinity, tenant isolation. Policies are represented as ordered rules: match -> score -> route.

Design tradeoffs that inform the runbook:
- Quick rollback vs consistent state: pushing a global policy rollback is fast but risks transient oscillation while proxies reconcile. Prefer targeted circuit-breaker toggles when possible.
- Local failover vs cross-region: cross-region traffic reduces latency guarantees for some tenants. Use region-failover for SLO-critical traffic only after cache-warming steps.

Decision matrix (condensed):
- Trigger: region p99 latency > 2.0s for 5m AND error-rate > 1% => Action: mark region degraded, route 25% -> other regions, enable short-circuit cache for warm prefixes.
- Trigger: control-plane push failing (push error rate > 0.5% for 3m) => Action: pause new policy rollouts, revert last push if it was live < 10m, enable proxy-local sticky fallback.
- Trigger: sustained GPU capacity shortage (util > 90% for 10m) => Action: route non-SLO traffic to lower-cost model variants or burst to Dedicated pools if reserved capacity available.

Incident scenarios and runbook steps (actionable):
SCENARIO A: Regional control plane partition (region R1 cannot reach control plane leader)
Detection signals:
  - Missing heartbeat from control-plane-agent in R1 (alert CP-AGENT-HEARTBEAT-MISSING).
  - Per-region health score drops to UNKNOWN.
  - Increased proxy miss rate for policy fetches and a spike in local fallback decisions.
Immediate triage (first 10 minutes):
  1) Page on-call, post to #platform-ops with details and initial timeline.
  2) Execute quick check: curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/health?region=R1 (use jump-host if needed).
  3) If control-plane API unresponsive from R1 but reachable from other regions, set region R1 to DEGRADED in the control UI with runbook reason tag: "network_partition_local".
Mitigation steps (fast safe toggles):
  - Toggle read-only-policy-mode for R1:
    curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/regions/R1/actions -d '{"action":"set_mode","mode":"read_only"}'
  - Enable proxy-local-fallback on R1 with a TTL of 30s to avoid runaway stale policy acceptance.
  - Adjust routing traffic weights: route 30% of SLO-critical traffic from R1 -> R2 and R3 using the traffic-router API.
Verification:
  - Check p50/p95/p99 latencies on SLO dashboards for affected customers.
  - Confirm heartbeat resumes or remains missing. If heartbeats remain missing > 20m escalate to network infra and include traceroute outputs.
Post-incident notes:
  - Record the push ID and policy bundle hash that was in use.
  - Add a follow-up test to replay a controlled policy push to R1 after network recovery.

SCENARIO B: Control-plane push causes routing oscillation (rollout-induced instability)
Detection signals:
  - Spikes in policy-change events across many proxies in a short window.
  - Elevated 429/503 from edge proxies as they re-evaluate policies.
  - Observed routing flaps in traffic logs (rapid alternation between routes for same session).
Immediate triage (first 5 minutes):
  1) Identify the push ID (control plane audit logs).
  2) Pause automated rollouts: set rollout-pause=true via admin console or API.
Mitigation steps (safe order):
  - If push age < 15m and rollout paused, revert to previous stable bundle:
    curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/rollouts/{push_id}/revert -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
  - If revert fails or is slow, opt for targeted rule-level disablement: apply an override that forces proxies to ignore the last N rules (admin-override).
  - Throttle policy propagation: set propagation-rate-limit to 5 bundles/min until stability.
Verification:
  - Confirm that policy-change rate normalizes and 429/503 rates fall to baseline.
  - Run a small synthetic traffic sweep that hits affected routes and validate consistent routing decisions across 90% of requests.
Post-incident:
  - Create ENG ticket with stack traces and the offending rule set.
  - Add guardrails: require two approvers for any policy that modifies cross-region route weights.

SCENARIO C: Degraded inference pool in a region (GPU shortage causing higher tail latency)
Detection signals:
  - Worker eviction events, OOM logs, or vertical autoscaler alerts.
  - p99 latency increase and increased inference timeouts.
Immediate triage:
  1) Identify affected model variants and tenants via the model-serving dashboard.
  2) If a single model variant is overloaded, activate model-variant-fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant for background traffic.
Mitigation steps:
  - Route low-priority tenants away from the overloaded pool:
    POST https://traffic-router.internal/api/v1/shifts -d '{"from_region":"R1","to_region":"R2","percent":40,"reason":"gpu_shortage"}'
  - If reserved Dedicated capacity exists, enable burst policy for 20 minutes: control UI -> capacity -> burst -> +20% (auth required).
  - Consider temporary autoscaler scale-up if cloud quota allows.
Verification:
  - Worker utilization drops to <75% and p99 latency returns under SLO threshold.
  - KV cache warmup metrics: track warm-key hit-rate on destination region to ensure QPS doesn't spike initial tail.
Post-incident:
  - Run a capacity test to validate autoscaler thresholds and increase baseline pool size if needed.

SCENARIO D: Control-plane split-brain (two leaders elect; conflicting policies)
Detection signals:
  - Conflicting policy bundle hashes observed by proxies.
  - Duplicate leader election logs and clients seeing different authoritative timestamps.
Immediate triage:
  1) Freeze new leader elections by setting leader-elections=disabled via control plane bootstrap override (requires quorum safeguards).
  2) Notify core infra and database team. This is an escalated event.
Mitigation (ordered):
  - Step 1: Isolate regions to prevent further divergence (mark one set as read-only).
  - Step 2: Identify the most recent consistent bundle by comparing hashes across majority of proxies.
  - Step 3: Force consensus rollback to that bundle, re-start leader election with maintenance window.
Verification:
  - Single leader in logs, consistent bundle hash across >80% proxies.
  - No further policy divergence for 30 minutes.
Post-incident:
  - Full RAID-style postmortem and database integrity checks.

Safe toggles cheat-sheet (quick reference):
- Mark-region-DEGRADED (control-plane API) => routes only SLO-critical traffic out.
- Read-only-policy-mode => proxies stop accepting new policy writes but continue serving existing rules.
- Proxy-local-fallback => enable short TTL fallback to last-good-bundle.
- Rollout-pause => stops dynamic rollouts immediately.
- Model-variant-fallback => fallback to quantized/cheaper variants for non-SLO tenants.

Testing & simulation plan (rehearsals):
- Quarterly tabletop: run a 60-minute exercise covering SCENARIO A and B. Verify runbook steps and communications.
- Controlled chaos test: simulate policy-push failures in staging with synthetic traffic that mirrors production percentiles. Run a sweep for the propagation-rate-limit behavior.
- Synthetic traffic templates: include cold-prefill sequences to measure KV cache warmup time; include sticky session flows to validate session affinity under weighted routing.
- Metrics to collect during tests: p50/p95/p99 latencies, policy-change events/min, 429/503 rates, policy bundle reconciliation time, KV warm-key hit-rate.

On-call communication template (paste to Slack when paging):
- Subject: [P1] Region R1 control-plane partition - {short description}
- What we see: heartbeats missing since <time>, p99 latency x ms, affected tenants list (short).
- Actions taken: marked R1 DEGRADED, shifted 30% traffic to R2/R3, enabled read-only-policy-mode.
- Next steps: network team engaged, checking control-plane logs.

Post-incident checklist (must-do before close):
- Attach logs and policy bundle hashes to Jira ticket (ENG-####).
- Run a validation push in a canary region and confirm no regression for 24 hours.
- Update playbook with discovered thresholds or new safe toggles.
- Schedule a retro with implicated teams and produce blameless action items.

Appendix: example investigative commands
- Check agent heartbeat from jump-host:
  ssh jump@ops-redwood 'curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/health?region=R1'
- Query policy bundles and hashes:
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/bundles?region=R2
- Adjust rollout pause:
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/admin/rollout -d '{"action":"pause"}'

Notes / open questions:
- Should we make rollback automatic when 5xx or 4xx rates cross X for N minutes? Current consensus: no automatic rollback for cross-region policies; require manual confirm.
- KV cache warmup remains the biggest source of tail SLO regressions during cross-region failovers. We should schedule a follow-up to evaluate pre-warming hooks and statically pinned prefixes for top-traffic tenants.

Author notes:
- This file combines runbook procedures with the architecture rationale to make triage decisions less ad-hoc. It intentionally errs on conservative toggles (pause before revert) to reduce cascading effects.
- Planned next steps: add pre-approved single-click actions in the console for common mitigations (mark-region, rollout-pause, proxy-fallback) with RBAC gating.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-08: initial draft (Aisha).
- 2025-12-12: added scenario C (gpu shortage) and test templates (Liam).
- 2026-02-20: clarified split-brain procedures and added rollback guardrails (Marta).

End of doc.
